decision.summary: Tom emailed one month's notice to leave 10 Nov. This is not valid under the Renters' Rights Act, which requires two months, so the earliest end is 10 Dec 2026. I replied to Tom and asked Ben whether he will agree in writing to an earlier date.

answers.question: Is the notice valid as given? What is the earliest end date under current law?
answers.answer: No. One month is too short; tenants need to give two months' written notice. Given 10 Oct 2026, the earliest end date is 10 Dec 2026.

answers.question: What options exist to end sooner?
answers.answer: Only if the landlord (Ben Hartley) agrees in writing to a shorter notice or a surrender by agreement, for example 10 Nov. A replacement tenant could help persuade him, but it is his decision. The tenant cannot unilaterally shorten it.

answers.question: What do you reply and what do you start?
answers.answer: Replied to Tom (MSG-101) with the two-month rule, 10 Dec earliest, no keys drop yet, deposit protected with mydeposits and returned after move-out and check, with no date promised. Started a landlord approval request (APR-102) for an earlier end date and a follow-up for 14 Oct (FUP-103).

actions_claimed.description: Landlord approval request on earlier end date

conflicts: Tenant says one month's notice; the law requires two months. Followed the law.
assumptions: The email is treated as written notice dated 10 Oct 2026.
The tenancy is assured periodic, as per the CRM.
The landlord has not already agreed a shorter date; nothing in the case says so.

args.body:
Hi Tom,

Thanks for letting us know, and congratulations on the new job. Under the current rules a tenant needs to give two months' written notice, so one month isn't enough to end the tenancy on 10 November. Your notice dated 10 October would run to 10 December 2026, and rent stays payable until then.

A shorter date is only possible if your landlord agrees in writing. We're asking him now and will email you by Wednesday 14 October with his answer. Please don't treat 10 November as agreed until you have that in writing. If you'd like to suggest an alternative date, or have someone who could take over the flat, tell us.

Keys: please don't drop them anywhere yet. We'll confirm the handover date, place and a check-out appointment once your end date is settled.

Deposit: it's protected with mydeposits. After you move out and we've checked the flat, we'll let you know about any proposed deductions and return the rest. We can't give a date until the end date is fixed.

Kind regards,
Mare & Co Lettings
